scalars.scalar_value: A combination of education, training, and experience that could provide the desired skills, knowledge and abilities may be considered. A typical way to obtain the required qualifications would be equivalent to an associate degree from an accredited college with major coursework in computer science, business administration, or a related field AND five (5) years of increasingly responsible experience in information technology including one (1) year of lead or supervisory experience.

A District on-line application on http://hr.fhda.edu/careers/. *In the application, you will provide information, which demonstrates your understanding of, sensitivity to, and respect for the diverse academic, socio-economic, ethnic, religious, and cultural backgrounds, disability, and sexual orientation of community college students, faculty and staff. Additionally, you will be asked to explain how your life experiences, studies or work have influenced your commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion.

items.item_text: A combination of education, training, and experience that could provide the desired skills, knowledge and abilities may be considered. A typical way to obtain the required qualifications would be equivalent to an associate degree from an accredited college with major coursework in computer science, business administration, or a related field AND five (5) years of increasingly responsible experience in information technology including one (1) year of lead or supervisory experience.

A District on-line application on http://hr.fhda.edu/careers/. *In the application, you will provide information, which demonstrates your understanding of, sensitivity to, and respect for the diverse academic, socio-economic, ethnic, religious, and cultural backgrounds, disability, and sexual orientation of community college students, faculty and staff. Additionally, you will be asked to explain how your life experiences, studies or work have influenced your commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion.
A current resume of all work experience, formal education and training.
Principles and practices of employee supervision, including work planning, assignment review and evaluation, discipline, and the training of staff in work procedures.
Select and supervise staff, provide training and development opportunities, ensure work is performed effectively, and evaluate performance in an objective and positive manner.
Principles and practices of leadership.
Assist in developing and implementing goals, objectives, practices, policies, procedures, and work standards.
Principles and techniques for working with groups and fostering effective team interaction to ensure teamwork is conducted smoothly.
Prepare and administer budgets and contracts; allocate limited resources in a cost-effective manner.
Basic principles and practices of budget administration and monitoring.
Research and evaluate new service delivery methods, procedures, and techniques.

Operations, services, and activities of educational technology systems, including a diverse range of computers, hardware, software, network systems, applications, mobile devices, multimedia equipment, security systems, and/or communication platforms.
Supervise and perform complex functions in the installation, implementation, testing, and integration of a variety of educational technology systems, hardware and software, and infrastructure.
Principles, practices, methods, and techniques of installing, configuring, troubleshooting, and maintaining hardware, software, and educational technology infrastructure and systems.
Supervise and perform advanced analyses of informational requirements and needs, identify problems, provide technical advice and consultation, and ensure efficient system utilization.
Security and monitoring devices, along with procedures essential for maintaining data integrity and security in networked systems.
Integrate information systems needs of diverse departments with District-wide educational technology systems, infrastructure, and policies, procedures, and standards.
Database principles and practices, including database management and administration.
Establish and maintain a variety of filing, record keeping, and reporting systems.
Basic principles of project management.
Understand, interpret, and apply all pertinent laws, codes, regulations, policies and procedures, and standards relevant to work performed.
Principles and practices of research and data collection.
Prepare clear and concise reports, correspondence, documentation, and other written materials.
Basic math and statistical techniques.
Use tact, initiative, prudence, and independent judgment within general policy and procedural guidelines.
Methods and techniques of preparing reports and general business correspondence.
Independently organize work, set priorities, meet critical deadlines, and follow-up on assignments.
Principles and procedures of record keeping.
Establish, maintain, and foster positive and effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.
Applicable federal, state, and local laws, codes, and regulations as well as industry standards and best practices pertinent to the assigned area of responsibility.
Effectively use computer systems, software applications relevant to work performed, and modern business equipment to perform a variety of work tasks.
The structure and content of the English language, including the meaning and spelling of words, rules of composition, and grammar.
A cover letter addressing your qualifications for the position.
Modern equipment and communication tools used for business functions and program, project, and task coordination, including computers and software programs relevant to work performed.

Techniques for providing a high level of customer service by effectively dealing with the public, students, and District staff, including individuals of diverse academic, socio-economic, ethnic, religious, and cultural backgrounds, disability, and sexual orientation.

Demonstrate understanding of, sensitivity to, and respect for the diverse academic, socio-economic, ethnic, religious, and cultural backgrounds, disability, and sexual orientation of community college students, faculty, and staff.
Communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing, using appropriate English grammar and syntax.

Understanding of, sensitivity to, and respect for the diverse academic, socio-economic, ethnic, religious, and cultural backgrounds, disability, and sexual orientation of community college students, faculty and staff.
